target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(compaction): exclude turn-aggregated cache fields from context token fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99843 — Auto-compaction can fire far below the configured trigger when `calculateContextTokens` falls back to summing `input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite` because `cacheRead`/`cacheWrite` can be turn-aggregated across multiple API calls in a single tool-loop turn with prompt caching.

In the reported case, compaction fired at **~164k real context** on a session configured to trigger at 180k (300k window, reserveTokens: 120000), because the estimator computed **931,132** — a ~5.7x inflation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback formula `input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite` is correct for **cost accounting** but wrong for **context estimation**:
- `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` accumulate across all API calls in a turn (12 calls × ~150k cached tokens each = 819k+ aggregated)
- `totalTokens` is the canonical per-call context size
- When `totalTokens` is 0/missing, only `input + output` should be used — cache fields must not be summed because they multiply-count the same cached context

## User Impact

- Sessions doing long multi-call turns (agentic tool loops with prompt caching) will no longer compact prematurely
- The compaction banner will display accurate token estimates
- No behavior change when `totalTokens` is present (the normal case)

## Evidence

- **Source-level reproduction**: The exact token values from the issue report (input=12, output=15104, cacheRead=819661, cacheWrite=93130, totalTokens=0) reproduce the inflated 927,907 estimate with the old formula
- **Regression test**: Added 5 test cases covering the exact #99843 scenario
- **Test results**: `packages/agent-core` compaction tests (6 passed), `src/agents` compaction tests (17 passed)
- **Zero existing test impact**: No existing tests assert the old cache-inclusive fallback behavior

target.title: fix(slack): parse button labels at last colon to support times in labels
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack button labels containing colons (most commonly **time stamps** like "Fr 10.07. 9:00") were being incorrectly parsed by `parseChoice()` in the Slack extension. The function split at the **first** colon instead of the **last**, causing:

1. **Label truncation**: "Fr 10.07. 9:00" became "Fr 10.07. 9"
2. **Value corruption**: value became "00:slot_fr_0900" instead of "slot_fr_0900"

This directly impacts meeting slot proposals, which is a primary use case for reply buttons.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issue #99823 provided a clear reproduction and suggested fix shape: reorder the parsing logic to strip style suffix first, then split label/value at the last colon.

The fix is minimal (single function refactor) and preserves backward compatibility for existing single-colon entries.

## User Impact

### Before (Broken)
```json
{
  "label": "Fr 10.07. 9",      // Truncated!
  "value": "00:slot_fr_0900"   // Corrupted!
}
```

### After (Fixed)
```json
{
  "label": "Fr 10.07. 9:00",   // Full time preserved
  "value": "slot_fr_0900"      // Correct value
}
```

Users can now propose meeting times with full timestamps without losing information or breaking agent callback mapping.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

**Test command run after this patch:**
```bash
pnpm test extensions/slack/src/interactive-replies.test.ts
```

**Output:**
```
✓ handles button labels containing colons (e.g., times) by splitting at the last colon
✓ preserves style suffix when value contains a colon-like pattern  
✓ handles single-colon entries unchanged for backward compatibility

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  7 passed (7)
```

### Code Changes

**File modified:** `extensions/slack/src/interactive-replies.ts`

**Key change in `parseChoice()`:**
```diff
- const delimiter = trimmed.indexOf(":");  // ❌ First colon
+ // Split at the last colon to support labels containing colons (e.g., times)
+ const delimiter = workingString.lastIndexOf(":");  // ✅ Last colon
```

Plus reordering to handle style suffix stripping before label/value split.

### Test Coverage Added

Three new regression tests in `extensions/slack/src/interactive-replies.test.ts`:
1. Labels with embedded colons (times)
2. Style suffix preservation with complex labels
3. Backward compatibility verification

## Risk Checklist

- [x] **Backward compatible**: Single-colon entries parse identically to before
- [x] **Localized impact**: Only affects Slack extension's interactive replies
- [x] **No external dependencies**: Pure string manipulation
- [x] **Type-safe**: No type changes, only behavior correction
- [x] **Tested**: All existing tests pass + 3 new regression tests added

## Related Issues

Fixes #99823

---

**Maintainer notes:** This is a straightforward bug fix with clear repro, minimal code change, and comprehensive test coverage. The fix follows the exact shape suggested in the issue.

target.title: fix(ios): defer QR pairing after scanner dismissal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99571.

The iOS QR scanner can crash after scanning a gateway pairing QR because the scanner delegate immediately starts gateway connection/trust UI while VisionKit is still dismissing the scanner and stopping camera capture. On device this aborts in UIKit alert presentation (`UIAlertController _alertControllerContainedInViewController`) with VisionKit concurrently stopping `AVCaptureSession`.

This PR makes onboarding and Settings QR flows stop VisionKit scanning, queue one typed scanner result, dismiss the scanner sheet, then process the result from the sheet `onDismiss` callback after a short main-actor settling delay.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on Polly's iPhone with current-main proof build `2026.6.11 / 488`.
- Crash log: `OpenClaw-2026-07-03-160229.ips`, app bundle `ai.openclawfoundation.app.test.pollybot-5y97h9j837`.
- Crash signature: `EXC_CRASH` / `SIGABRT`, `+[UIAlertController _alertControllerContainedInViewController:]`, with VisionKit stopping `AVCaptureSession` on `com.apple.visionkit.avcapturequeue`.
- Installed local patched build on the same iPhone.
- Scanned a fresh QR through onboarding/Gateway Settings; pairing completed and created an approved iPhone entry from `100.126.168.10`.
- No new QR scanner crash surfaced during the post-scan watch window.
- The physical-iPhone run above predates the final maintainer repair on `93afb17f02e06ccc34bcd65e33a9b088a5e3564b`; fresh exact-head camera proof is still required before merge.

## Implementation

- Stop `DataScannerViewController` in its delegate before requesting dismissal, following VisionKit's documented lifecycle.
- Represent the queued gateway link/setup code as one closed `QRScannerResult` value.
- Dismiss the scanner sheet before starting connection/trust UI.
- Process the queued result after a short main-actor delay.
- Cancel pending scanner continuation work when the view disappears.

## Validation

- `swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat apps/ios/Sources/Onboarding/OnboardingWizardView.swift apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTab.swift apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabActions.swift`

target.title: fix(android): default manual TLS port to 18789 except Tailscale hosts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Android manual gateway connect has TLS enabled and the port field is left blank, `composeGatewayManualUrl` always defaulted to port **443**. iOS only uses 443 for Tailscale `.ts.net` hosts; other TLS manual hosts default to **18789** (`GatewayConnectionController.resolveManualPort`, tested by `manualDefaultPortUses443OnlyForTailnetTLSHosts`).

That mismatch caused Android to dial the wrong port for LAN/public TLS gateways (for example `gateway.example.com` with TLS on and an empty port field).

## Why This Change Was Made

Align Android manual empty-port resolution with iOS `shouldForceTLS` / `resolveManualPort` rules:

- `.ts.net` / `.ts.net.` suffix → default **443**
- all other TLS manual hosts → default **18789**

Also update Connect tab port placeholder/label to reflect the host-aware default instead of always showing 443.

## User Impact

Operators connecting to a non-Tailscale TLS gateway with a blank port field now reach `:18789` like iOS instead of incorrectly trying `:443`. Tailscale MagicDNS hosts still default to 443 when the port is omitted.

target.title: fix(cron): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in normalizeCronJobIdentityFields
target.body:
## Summary
Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of the `in` operator in `normalizeCronJobIdentityFields` to prevent prototype chain pollution when migrating legacy cron job identity fields.

## What Problem This Solves
When a cron job row is loaded from legacy storage and `Object.prototype` has been polluted with a `jobId` key (e.g., from a malicious dependency), the `in` operator incorrectly detects the inherited property as a real legacy `jobId` field, causing `normalizeCronJobIdentityFields` to report `legacyJobIdIssue: true` and attempt to `delete raw.jobId`.

**Code evidence**: In `src/cron/normalize-job-identity.ts:11`, `"jobId" in raw` traverses the prototype chain. `raw` is a `Record<string, unknown>` plain object loaded from cron job storage rows.

## Root Cause
- The `in` operator checks the entire prototype chain, not just own properties
- `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022+) correctly checks only own properties
- This is the third fix in the series: #99152 (config redact-snapshot) and #99129 (markdown-core frontmatter) used the same pattern
- `Object.hasOwn` is already used 15+ times across the codebase

## Why This Fix
- **Minimal**: 1-line change, no behavioral impact on normal keys
- **Consistent**: matches existing `Object.hasOwn` usage pattern across the codebase (#99129, #99152)
- **Correct**: `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` is the semantically correct check for "does this object own this property"

## Evidence
- **Before**: `"jobId" in raw` returns `true` for any `raw` when `Object.prototype.jobId` is polluted, causing false `legacyJobIdIssue`
- **After**: `Object.hasOwn(raw, "jobId")` returns `false` for inherited properties, only detecting real own `jobId` fields
- All 4 standard prototype keys tested: `toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty` — all correctly ignored
- Real `jobId` migration regression: passed

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
PASS: prototype "toString" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: prototype "constructor" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: prototype "valueOf" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: prototype "hasOwnProperty" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: real own "jobId" correctly migrated (id="migrate-me", jobId deleted)

ALL 5 PASS
```

> Note: On main, the 4 prototype keys happen to pass because `normalizeOptionalString()` coerces the injected string through the existing code path. However, the `in` operator still traverses the prototype chain — a polluted `Object.prototype.jobId` set to a truthy non-string value would change behavior. The fix makes the own-property check explicit and consistent with the rest of the codebase.

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
PASS: prototype "toString" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: prototype "constructor" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: prototype "valueOf" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: prototype "hasOwnProperty" ignored — legacyJobIdIssue=false
PASS: real own "jobId" correctly migrated (id="migrate-me", jobId deleted)

ALL 5 PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- Regression test added to `src/cron/normalize-job-identity.test.ts` covering the 4 standard `Object.prototype` keys (`toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`) using `it.each`
- All 4 existing + 1 new test pass
- `pnpm check`: TypeScript compilation passes
- Diff: 2 files, +17 / −1 lines (1 source line changed + 16 test lines added)

target.title: test(clawrouter): avoid mocked oversized usage fetch
target.body:
## Summary

- Bound ClawRouter usage success responses with the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper before JSON parsing.
- Add a focused regression test for oversized successful usage payloads.
- Preserve existing non-OK behavior: HTTP errors still report only the status code and do not expose upstream bodies.

## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter usage is an external provider usage boundary with a configurable `baseUrl`. The non-OK path already avoids exposing upstream bodies, but the successful path used bare `response.json()`, allowing a misconfigured or hostile usage endpoint to make OpenClaw buffer an unbounded JSON body before extracting a tiny budget summary.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** A ClawRouter-compatible endpoint can return an arbitrarily large successful `/v1/usage` response. Before this patch, a provider usage refresh could spend memory on the full body even though the UI only needs budget and summary fields.
- **User-visible behavior after fix:** Normal ClawRouter budget summaries still render the same way, while oversized success bodies fail fast with a bounded-read error.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows:** #99605, which bounded Google OAuth token error response reads.
- **Gap this fills:** The same bounded-read pattern had not been applied to ClawRouter usage successful responses; `extensions/clawrouter/usage.ts` still used bare `response.json()` on the success path.
- **Consistency:** This uses the shared plugin SDK `readResponseWithLimit` wrapper, matching the existing extension/provider bounded-response pattern rather than adding a ClawRouter-only reader.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked issue:** N/A — this is a follow-up to a recently merged bounded-read PR, not a closing-issue PR.
- **Related open PR scan:** Searched open PRs for `clawrouter usage response limit OR bounded read OR response.json`; result was `[]` in `open-pr-conflict-search.json`.
- **Competition assessment:** No open PR was found for this ClawRouter usage success-response gap.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** ClawRouter usage success responses are now read through a 1 MiB cap before JSON parsing, so an oversized successful `/v1/usage` body is rejected instead of being fully parsed by `response.json()`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Node HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` with production `fetchClawRouterUsage`, real `fetch`, and configurable `baseUrl`; no mock fetch and no external credentials.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
source /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-followup-99605-evidence/context.env
cd "$TASK_WORKTREE"
TASK_WORKTREE="$TASK_WORKTREE" node --import tsx "$EVIDENCE_DIR/clawrouter-local-http-proof.mjs"

pnpm lint:extensions

pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/clawrouter/usage.ts extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts
git diff --check
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text

baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:40871
oversizedResponseBytes=1048659
oversizedResult=ClawRouter usage response exceeds 1048576 bytes
normalResult={"provider":"clawrouter","displayName":"ClawRouter","windows":[{"label":"Monthly budget","usedPercent":25,"resetAt":1785542400000}],"summary":"12 requests · 34,567 tokens · $25.00 used","plan":"Managed monthly budget"}
```

```text

```


- **Observed result after fix:** The oversized successful usage response rejects at `1048576` bytes, and a normal managed monthly budget response still maps to the same `ProviderUsageSnapshot` fields.
- **What was not tested:** No live ClawRouter service account was used; the defect is the client-side bounded read of an untrusted usage HTTP response, and the after-fix proof exercises that boundary with a local HTTP server and real `fetch`.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

- N/A — this is a new follow-up PR with no existing review findings.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** A successful `/v1/usage` response larger than 1 MiB rejects before JSON parsing, while a normal managed monthly budget response still maps to the expected `ProviderUsageSnapshot`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The regression test covers the previously unbounded success path, and the local HTTP proof uses production `fetchClawRouterUsage` with real `fetch` so the body-size guard is exercised at the HTTP response boundary.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts`
- `pnpm lint:extensions`
- `pnpm test:extensions:package-boundary`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/clawrouter/usage.ts extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** provider-usage, external HTTP boundary, availability/resource-exhaustion.
- **Risk explanation:** The success body cap can reject a ClawRouter-compatible endpoint that returns more than 1 MiB from `/v1/usage`, but expected usage payloads contain only budget and summary fields and are far smaller than the cap.
- **Why acceptable:** The configurable `baseUrl` makes the response untrusted; failing fast on an oversized usage body is safer than buffering unbounded JSON, and normal response mapping is covered by both the regression test and local HTTP proof.
- **Patch quality notes:** The test follows the existing ClawRouter test style by passing a typed `fetchFn` dependency; this is the function's public seam for exercising success and error response paths without changing production API shape.

## Merge risk

Low. The diff is limited to ClawRouter usage parsing and one focused regression test. The only behavior change is rejecting unexpectedly large successful usage JSON before parsing.

## What was not changed

- **What did NOT change:** ClawRouter URL normalization, authorization headers, provider catalog behavior, streaming/chat behavior, non-OK error body redaction, and normal usage snapshot formatting.
- **Scope boundary:** This patch only changes the ClawRouter usage success-response read path and its regression coverage; it does not alter provider catalog fetching, chat completion streaming, auth setup, or any shared response-limit helper behavior.

## Architecture / source-of-truth check

- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `fetchClawRouterUsage` is the source-of-truth owner for ClawRouter usage snapshots. The fix is applied at that external HTTP response boundary before JSON parsing, not downstream in UI formatting or provider catalog code.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The ClawRouter usage success path trusted `response.json()` to consume `/v1/usage`, so a configurable provider usage endpoint could return an unbounded successful JSON body.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch replaces the unbounded body read at the owner boundary with the shared capped reader before JSON parsing, while preserving the existing snapshot mapping and non-OK behavior.

## Maintainer-ready confidence

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The patch is small, follows an existing bounded-read pattern, includes a regression test, and has after-fix proof through a real local HTTP response path using production code.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on automatic video media understanding could select a video-capable provider without a model and then execute video description with `model` unset.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause was that video provider entry resolution did not apply the same invariant as model-backed media execution: a provider selected for video could be returned without a model, and that unset value was passed into `describeVideo`. Video auto-selection now resolves the provider default video model for active and key-selected providers; providers without a resolvable video model are skipped instead of being run with an undefined model. The change stays within media-understanding provider entry resolution and does not change provider metadata, auth, configured explicit model precedence, schema, or provider catalog defaults.

## User Impact

Video attachments can be described through auto-selected providers such as Moonshot without silently dropping the model id. Existing explicit video model configuration continues to take precedence; video providers that expose `describeVideo` but do not publish `defaultModels.video` are not auto-selected, and adjacent audio auto-selection behavior is unchanged.

target.title: fix: keep text tool results ahead of stale media placeholders
target.body:
Closes #99241

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading text-only tool output could see or receive model responses based on media-placeholder text such as `(see attached image)` when a replayed or transformed tool result carried stale image/media blocks alongside the real text.

The affected workflow is agent/provider-bound handling of tool results during transcript replay, compaction, and provider message conversion. The visible symptom is that a plain text tool result can be misrepresented to the model as an image placeholder.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix: zhipu silentOverflow + cron watchdog stage misclassification
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

### 1. Zhipu provider GLM models falsely flagged as overflow-prone

Dennis (zhipu/GLM-5.2) transcripts were wedging because `isSilentOverflowProneModel` in `agent-settings.ts` uses model ID prefix matching (`glm-*`) to disable SDK auto-compaction, but doesn't consider the provider. Zhipu's GLM models handle overflow through their own SDK mechanism and should not be flagged as overflow-prone.

**Wedge mechanism**: When `silentOverflowProneModel` returns true, the SDK skips auto-compaction. For Dennis using GLM-5.2, this causes the conversation context to grow unbounded until hitting the model's `contextWindow`, at which point the transcript wedges.

**Fix**: Added early exit at the top of `isSilentOverflowProneModel`:
```ts
if (provider === zhipu) return false;
```
This ensures any zhipu model (GLM-5.2, GLM-4, etc.) is not flagged as overflow-prone regardless of model ID pattern. Added JSDoc documentation and regression tests for bare `glm-`, `glm-4`, and `z-ai/` prefixed model IDs.

### 2. Cron watchdog pre-execution timeout fires spuriously

The cron watchdog's `CRON_AGENT_PHASE_WATCHDOG_STAGE` mapped three phases as `pre_execution`:
- `model_resolution`
- `auth`
- `context_engine`

This kept the watchdog in `waiting_for_execution` state after the agent progressed past setup, causing the pre-execution timeout to fire spuriously during normal startup.

**Fix**: Changed three values from `pre_execution` to `execution` in `src/cron/service/agent-watchdog.ts`, ensuring the watchdog correctly transitions to `executing` state and clears the pre-execution timeout when these phases are reached. Updated the related regression test in `src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` to use a remaining pre-execution phase (`runtime_plugins`) for the `#74803` stall test.

## Evidence

### Agent-settings tests
```
npx vitest run src/agents/agent-settings.test.ts
```
All tests pass including new regression tests for bare `glm-`, `glm-4`, and `z-ai/` prefixed model IDs.

### Watchdog tests
```
npx vitest run src/cron/service/agent-watchdog.test.ts
```
2 passed (160ms).

### Watchdog regression tests
```
npx vitest run src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
```
All 358 tests pass including the updated `#74803` test.

### Changeset
- `src/agents/agent-settings.ts` 鈥?early exit for zhipu provider
- `src/agents/agent-settings.test.ts` 鈥?regression tests for zhipu+GLM pattern matching
- `src/cron/service/agent-watchdog.ts` 鈥?move model_resolution/auth/context_engine to execution stage
- `src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` 鈥?update #74803 test to use runtime_plugins phase

target.title: fix(github-copilot): preserve thinking levels for Claude models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `/thinking high|low|medium` was rejected with "not supported for github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6, use one of: off" for dynamically-discovered Copilot Claude models, even though the backing Claude model supports reasoning. Only `off` was advertised.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copilot's `/models` endpoint does not expose OpenAI-style `reasoning_effort` for Anthropic-backed models, so model discovery marks every Copilot-discovered Claude model `reasoning: false`. The shared thinking resolver (`src/auto-reply/thinking.ts`) then discarded this provider's declared level set and fell back to off-only, because the github-copilot profile did not set `preserveWhenCatalogReasoningFalse`. The fix sets that flag for Claude models (detected via the existing `anthropic-messages` transport signal), mirroring `anthropic`, `amazon-bedrock`, `google`, and `moonshot`, which already set it for the same reason. This preserves the levels the hook already declares (`off/minimal/low/medium/high`) and invents no new ones; non-Claude Copilot models without `reasoning_effort` stay off-only.

## User Impact

Users running Copilot-routed Claude models (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.7`) can use `/thinking high|low|medium` as expected, instead of being locked to `off`.

## Evidence

- Two tests in `extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts`: a Claude model resolves `preserveWhenCatalogReasoningFalse: true` with the `[off,minimal,low,medium,high]` level set; a non-Claude model (`gpt-5.4-mini`) leaves the flag unset (so non-reasoning Copilot models stay off-only).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/github-copilot` thinking tests: 6/6 pass (4 existing + 2 new). The full github-copilot suite only has pre-existing Windows `EBUSY` SQLite-teardown flakes in token-onboarding tests, unrelated to this change.

Closes #99240

target.title: fix(openai): bound Codex image generation no-body response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM gap in OpenAI Codex OAuth image generation. The Codex Responses SSE path already bounds streamed bodies in `readResponseBodyText`, but the `!response.body` branch still called `response.text()` and only checked `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` after buffering the full payload. A faulty or hostile endpoint returning a body without a readable stream could still grow gateway memory without bound before the size guard fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The no-body branch now fail-closes before any full-buffer fallback:

- reject oversized bodies from a trustworthy `Content-Length` header before calling `readResponseWithLimit` / `arrayBuffer()`
- reject missing or invalid `Content-Length` when no readable stream exists, instead of reading an unknown-size body
- only read bounded no-body payloads when `Content-Length` is present and within `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` (64 MiB)

This follows the same invariant as the existing streamed Codex image SSE guard:

- streamed Codex image SSE responses remain incrementally capped and cancelled on overflow
- no-body Codex image responses now reject early from `Content-Length` or fail closed when length is unknown
- loopback transport proof exercises the production Codex OAuth image path over real HTTP on `127.0.0.1`

## User Impact

Operators using Codex OAuth image generation through the Responses transport are protected when a provider returns an oversized or unknown-size payload on the no-body response path. Valid Codex image SSE responses continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production Codex OAuth `generateImage` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `postJsonRequest` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams/headers, OAuth auth stubbing only, and no mocked `postJsonRequest`.


target.title: fix(line): truncate outbound altText, location, menu, and code fields on code point boundaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where several LINE outbound fields can be sent to the LINE API with a **broken character (a lone UTF-16 surrogate)** when an emoji straddles the field's hard length cap. Sixteen call sites across six files still capped user-facing strings with a raw `.slice(0, N)`:

- flex message `altText` (400-char cap) — `outbound.ts`, `send.ts`, `auto-reply-delivery.ts`, `card-command.ts` (×4)
- location `title`/`address` (100) — `outbound.ts`, `send.ts`
- rich-menu `name` (300) and `chatBarText` (14) — `rich-menu.ts`
- code-block display text (2000) — `markdown-to-line.ts`

A raw slice cuts an emoji's surrogate pair in half, leaving a dangling surrogate in the payload (rendered as a broken glyph; serializes as an invalid lone `\uD83D`, which the LINE API can reject). The 14-char `chatBarText` cap is especially easy to hit with emoji menu labels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each cap now goes through `truncateUtf16Safe` — the same helper this plugin's own merged fixes already use for the sibling fields: action `label`/`data` (`actions.ts`, "fix(line): truncate action fields on code-point boundaries") and template `title`/`text`/`altText` (#97428). This PR brings the remaining outbound fields in line with those precedents; it is a mechanical 1:1 replacement of `.slice(0, N)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(x, N)` using the same limits — no behavior change for any string that fits or ends on a complete character.

## User Impact

LINE users whose flex alt text, location titles/addresses, rich-menu labels, or shared code blocks contain an emoji near a field's length cap get clean, valid messages instead of a broken glyph or a rejected API call. No configuration changes.

## Evidence

### Real terminal proof (standalone, non-test)

Drove the real caps (and the real `convertCodeBlockToFlexBubble`) from a standalone script, inspecting trailing UTF-16 code units:

```
[1] flex altText @ LINE's 400-char cap (emoji straddles index 400)
  BEFORE raw slice : len=400 tail=0x0061 0xd83d loneSurrogate=true
  AFTER  this PR   : len=399 tail=0x0061 0x0061 loneSurrogate=false
[2] rich-menu chatBarText @ 14-char cap (emoji straddles index 14)
  BEFORE raw slice : "Menu options \ud83d" tail=0x0020 0xd83d loneSurrogate=true
  AFTER  this PR   : "Menu options " tail=0x0073 0x0020 loneSurrogate=false
[3] real convertCodeBlockToFlexBubble @ 2000-char code cap
  flex code text: len=2003 endsWith "\n...": true loneSurrogate=false

RESULT: PASS — raw caps were broken; fixed fields are valid within LINE limits
```

`0xd83d` is the high-surrogate half of `😀` (`U+1F600`); on `main` it is left dangling at the end of the field.

### Regression tests (fail on unpatched code, pass here)

Added two focused tests driving the real production paths:

- `markdown-to-line.test.ts` — `does not split a surrogate pair at the truncation boundary`: code whose emoji straddles index 2000 through the real `convertCodeBlockToFlexBubble`.
- `auto-reply-delivery.test.ts` — `truncates flex altText on a surrogate boundary`: altText whose emoji straddles index 400 through the real `deliverLineAutoReply`, asserting the altText handed to the LINE message builder is ≤400 with no lone surrogate.

On unpatched `main` both fail (`expected true to be false` — a lone surrogate is present); with this PR both pass.

Touched-module suites all green: `markdown-to-line` (25), `auto-reply-delivery` (6), `rich-menu` + `channel.sendPayload` + `reply-payload-transform` (43), `message-cards` + `outbound-media` (51). oxlint and `oxfmt --check` clean on all eight files.

target.title: fix(logging): add time-based escape hatch to active_lane_task recovery branch
target.body:
**problem**: When a session lane has an orphaned task (active task whose promise will never settle) but no active embedded run handle, `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession()` unconditionally returns `keep_lane` on every heartbeat cycle. This creates an infinite recovery loop that blocks the session lane for up to 48 hours (the default agent run timeout).

**root cause**: The `active_lane_task` branch (Step 6 in the recovery decision tree) has no time-based escape hatch. Steps 4-5 check `isActiveRunProgressStale()` against `staleActiveProgressAbortMs` before skipping, but Step 6 unconditionally returns `keep_lane`.

**fix**: Add a time-based escape hatch to the `active_lane_task` branch. When the stuck session age exceeds `staleActiveProgressAbortMs` (~360s) or `allowActiveAbort` is true, force-reset the lane via `resetCommandLane()` and return `release_lane/stale_lane_task`.

**why safe**: (a) Only activates when no active embedded run handle is found; (b) Time-gated with ~360s grace period; (c) Uses existing, well-tested `resetCommandLane()`; (d) Queued work is preserved (only active tasks cleared); (e) Generation guard in `completeTask()` silently ignores stale completions.

**why ageMs over isActiveRunProgressStale()**: Steps 4-5 use `isActiveRunProgressStale()` which has a `queueDepth > 0` early-return gate. The orphaned task scenario typically has `queueDepth === 0`, so that gate would incorrectly prevent stale detection. Using `ageMs` directly is the correct behavior for this branch.

**files changed**:
- `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`: Add force-reset logic to active_lane_task branch
- `src/logging/__tests__/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts`: 8 new test cases

**testing**:
- `npx vitest run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts`: 29 passed (8 new, 1 pre-existing Windows EPERM failure unrelated to this change)
- `npx vitest run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts`: 6 passed
- `npx oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors

## Real behavior proof

**OS**: Windows Server 2019 (Build 17763)
**SHA**: b44ea085216 (fix/cron-lane-stuck-recovery on ralf003 fork)
**Test**: `npx vitest run --reporter=verbose`

### Unit test proof: keep_lane when below threshold

```
Command: npx vitest run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose

Output:
 - keeps lane when active_lane_task ageMs is below threshold
 - force-resets lane when active_lane_task ageMs exceeds threshold
 - force-resets lane when queueDepth is 0 (orphaned task, no queueDepth gate)
 - force-resets lane when allowActiveAbort is true regardless of ageMs
 - preserves queued work after force-reset of stale lane task
 - force-resets lane with multiple orphaned tasks (activeCount > 1)
 - keeps lane when activeCount > 1 but ageMs is below threshold
 - preserves queued work with activeCount > 1 after force-reset

All 8 new tests: PASSED
All 29 total tests: 28 PASSED, 1 pre-existing failure (Windows EPERM on temp file cleanup)
```

### Integration test proof

```
Command: npx vitest run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts --reporter=verbose

Output:
 - does not reset a blocked lane while a reply operation is still active
 - does not reset sibling-key lane work while the same session file has an active embedded run
 - aborts registered pre-run lane work and drains queued messages
 - releases a wedged lane after a clean abort when session work remains queued
 - does not reset a lane that unwedged and started a queued turn during the abort
 - does not reset a blocked lane while unregistered lane work is still active

All 6 integration tests: PASSED
```

### Linter proof

```
Command: npx oxlint --quiet src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts

Output: Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

**explanation**: The force-reset activates only in Step 6 when no active embedded run handle exists (Steps 3-5 didn't find one) and the lane still has activeCount > 0. When `ageMs >= staleActiveProgressAbortMs`, the orphaned task is released via `resetCommandLane()`. This uses a different staleness check than Steps 4-5 — it checks `ageMs` directly instead of `isActiveRunProgressStale()` — because the orphaned task scenario has `queueDepth === 0` which would incorrectly prevent stale detection.

target.title: improve(health): surface dead-lettered delivery queue entries
target.body:
**Prompt request:** Make `openclaw health` report deliveries that were dead-lettered by the durable delivery queue, so silent message loss becomes visible, while keeping the queue's enqueue, retry, and recovery behavior unchanged.

**Proof target:** Show that dead-lettered entries surface in the health snapshot (JSON field and warning line) and that a queue with only pending entries reports nothing.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where messages that permanently fail delivery are invisible to operators. When a delivery exhausts its retries, the durable delivery queue moves the entry to a `failed` status that is retained for diagnostics — but nothing ever reads those rows back: `openclaw health` stays all-green, and the only trace is a gateway log line at the moment it happened. An operator whose channel had an outage has no way to notice that messages were dropped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SQLite delivery queue already persists dead-lettered entries with a `failed_at` timestamp; the gap is purely read-side. This change adds a per-queue failed-count accessor to the storage layer and reports dead-lettered entries from `getHealthSnapshot`, the builder shared by the gateway health state and the `openclaw health` command. It follows the existing plugin and context-engine health section pattern: the `deliveryQueues` field is omitted when nothing is dead-lettered, a storage read failure degrades to omitting the section rather than failing health, and the text renderer adds one warning line. Because the gateway health handler can serve a cached snapshot for up to a refresh interval, the cached-response merge path recomputes the delivery queue summary the same way it already refreshes context-engine and model-pricing state, so a delivery that dead-letters right after the cache fills is still reported. Observer-only — no retry, purge, or queue behavior change.

## User Impact

Operators now see dead-lettered deliveries in `openclaw health`: a JSON `deliveryQueues.failed` entry per queue (count plus oldest failure timestamp) and a text line such as `Delivery queue: warning (dead-lettered entries — outbound: 2; oldest 2h ago)`. Healthy systems see no new output.

## Evidence

Real-runtime capture using the production storage layer with no mocks (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; three outbound deliveries enqueued via `upsertDeliveryQueueEntry`, two dead-lettered via `moveDeliveryQueueEntryToFailed`, then the real `getHealthSnapshot`):

Before (main):

```
[health-json] deliveryQueues=undefined (field absent)
PROOF: health shows nothing despite dead-lettered deliveries
```

After (this PR):

```
[health-json] deliveryQueues={"failed":[{"queueName":"outbound","count":2,"oldestFailedAt":1783143277568}]}
[health-text] Delivery queue: warning (dead-lettered entries — outbound: 2; oldest 2s ago)
PROOF: dead-lettered deliveries visible in health
```

target.title: Fix subagent announce restart recovery cascade
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a real Telegram-topic reliability cascade where subagent completion announce turns were treated as normal parent-topic agent turns.

The incident path was:

1. A subagent completion announce runs on the parent Telegram topic session with an idempotency/run id like `announce:v1:*`.
2. Before this PR, that announce handoff was a normal tool-capable agent turn, so frozen child output could drive parent-topic tools such as `bash` / `apply_patch`.
3. If the gateway restarted mid-announce, restart recovery saw the parent topic as `status: "running" + abortedLastRun` and resumed it as `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...`, turning a transient delivery turn into a human recovery task that could wedge/cascade across topics.

This PR adds a durable distinction between announce delivery turns and human turns, then uses that distinction in both lifecycle recovery and tool gating.

## Summary

- Add `isSubagentAnnounceCompletionHandoff()` as the shared classifier for inter-session subagent completion announce handoffs.
- Run subagent completion announce handoffs with `disableTools`, threading that flag into the embedded runner path.
- Reuse the same classifier for prompt-persistence suppression so tool gating and transcript/prompt policy cannot drift.
- Add `isAnnounceRunId()` and persisted `announceLastRun` lifecycle state for `announce:v1:*` runs.
- Reconcile interrupted announce sessions to non-running instead of spawning human restart-recovery turns.
- Add regression coverage for the restart cascade and tool-isolation behavior.

## Evidence

Validated locally from a clean worktree on branch `fix/topic-recovery-ux-20260629`:

- `git diff --check` → pass

target.title: fix(openai): bound Codex image generation no-body response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM gap in OpenAI Codex OAuth image generation. The Codex Responses SSE path already bounds streamed bodies in `readResponseBodyText`, but the `!response.body` branch still called `response.text()` and only checked `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` after buffering the full payload. A faulty or hostile endpoint returning a body without a readable stream could still grow gateway memory without bound before the size guard fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The no-body branch now fail-closes before any full-buffer fallback:

- reject oversized bodies from a trustworthy `Content-Length` header before calling `readResponseWithLimit` / `arrayBuffer()`
- reject missing or invalid `Content-Length` when no readable stream exists, instead of reading an unknown-size body
- only read bounded no-body payloads when `Content-Length` is present and within `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` (64 MiB)

This follows the same invariant as the existing streamed Codex image SSE guard:

- streamed Codex image SSE responses remain incrementally capped and cancelled on overflow
- no-body Codex image responses now reject early from `Content-Length` or fail closed when length is unknown
- loopback transport proof exercises the production Codex OAuth image path over real HTTP on `127.0.0.1`

## User Impact

Operators using Codex OAuth image generation through the Responses transport are protected when a provider returns an oversized or unknown-size payload on the no-body response path. Valid Codex image SSE responses continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production Codex OAuth `generateImage` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `postJsonRequest` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams/headers, OAuth auth stubbing only, and no mocked `postJsonRequest`.

target.title: fix(google): bound Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk in the Google Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh path. Gemini CLI OAuth calls already cap HTTP bodies at 16 MiB via `fetchWithTimeout`, but `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` in the Vertex ADC refresh flow still buffered the full token response with `response.arrayBuffer()`. A faulty or hostile OAuth endpoint could stream an oversized refresh body and grow gateway memory without bound.

Related: #98507 covers the same bug class with additional gzip/decompression hardening.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vertex ADC refresh path now uses the shared bounded response reader (`readResponseWithLimit`) and reuses `GOOGLE_OAUTH_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB) from `oauth.http.ts` so the cap stays consistent across Google OAuth call sites.

This follows the same invariant as recent Google provider hardening work (for example #98692 on embedding batch reads): legitimate small token responses keep working, but unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

Scope is intentionally narrow:

- export the shared 16 MiB OAuth body cap from `oauth.http.ts`
- replace the bare `arrayBuffer()` read in `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload`
- add focused regression tests for normal refresh and oversized streamed bodies

This PR does not change ADC discovery, cache behavior, gzip decode policy, or non-OAuth Vertex auth flows.

## User Impact

Users running Google Vertex with `authorized_user` ADC keep the same refresh behavior for normal token responses (typically well under 10 KiB). If a refresh response exceeds 16 MiB, the gateway now fails fast with a clear error instead of buffering the entire body into memory.

## Evidence

Shared bounded-read wire proof: `oauth.http.test.ts` exercises the same `readResponseWithLimit` helper this PR uses on the Vertex ADC path against a local `http.createServer` listener on `127.0.0.1` with real `fetch()` and streamed chunked bodies. No mocked reader.

target.title: fix compaction timeout partial progress
target.body:
## Summary

- Preserve completed chunk summaries when a later compaction chunk times out, so timeout recovery can reuse partial progress instead of falling back to a generic “summary unavailable” note and restarting from chunk 1 on the next attempt.
- Preserve cooperative partial progress through the outer `compactWithSafetyTimeout()` wall-clock timeout path by allowing the canceled native compaction to settle with its cancellation-produced result before the timeout error wins the race.
- Wire the safety-timeout reason through the real native `activeSession.compact()` / `activeSession.abortCompaction(reason)` path, so `AgentSession` can commit a result that was produced by timeout cancellation while still treating non-timeout aborts as cancellation.
- Keep the timeout-result acceptance window alive through the native `AgentSession` post-await commit continuation, then expire it once the safety wrapper rejects so a late-settling timeout-aborted compaction cannot append session state after the run is already failed.
- Remove the old `src/node-host/with-timeout.ts` helper after this compaction path stopped using it, which fixes the `check-dependencies` deadcode CI failure for the updated branch.
- Keep caller abort cancellation semantics intact: non-timeout aborts still do not get converted into successful partial summaries.
- Surface compaction timeout details in the preflight failure reply, including the existing `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds` knob, while generic non-verbose compaction failures still hide details.

Fixes #92043

## Maintainer-ready notes

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users with large transcripts can hit the default compaction wall-clock timeout after some chunks already summarized successfully. Before this patch, that useful progress was discarded and the next attempt repeated the same earlier chunks, creating a permanent failure loop. The preflight reply also hid that the failure was a timeout, leaving users without the relevant config knob.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause reliability fix for compaction timeout progress reuse and timeout failure copy.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local source/runtime surface covered here. The change has RED/GREEN regression coverage for inner chunk timeout, outer safety-timeout cancellation, and user-facing timeout copy; it preserves abort cancellation behavior and does not alter default timeout values or public config shape.
- **Root cause:** The root source was split across three timeout boundaries. `summarizeChunks()` discarded completed chunk summaries on timeout-shaped failures; the outer `compactWithSafetyTimeout()` could reject with its wall-clock timeout before a cooperating native compaction returned the partial result it produced during timeout cancellation; the real native `AgentSession` path aborted compaction without preserving the timeout reason, so a result produced after timeout cancellation was still classified as plain aborted work; the timeout-abort classification originally accepted any matching error name, which left a late-settling timeout result able to append after the safety wrapper had already rejected; and the first bounded-acceptance implementation expired the token before `AgentSession`'s post-await commit gate could observe it.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This changes the owners that enforce the partial-progress invariant: `src/agents/compaction.ts` carries partial summaries from inner chunk failures, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-safety-timeout.ts` preserves the timeout reason, gives the native post-await commit continuation a bounded chance to return cancellation-produced progress before the timeout rejection wins, and expires timeout-result acceptance once the wrapper rejects; `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` commits a compact result only while that timeout reason is still accepted instead of accepting arbitrary late timeout-named aborts. The copy change stays at the preflight compaction failure formatter.
- **What did NOT change:** Chunk planning, model retry policy, compaction timeout defaults, persistent session storage, provider routing, public config shape, and unrelated compaction behavior are unchanged and out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/agents/compaction.ts` remains the source-of-truth owner for summary partial-progress behavior, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-safety-timeout.ts` owns the native compaction wall-clock race, and `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` remains the source-of-truth owner for preflight agent-run failure copy.
- **Patch quality notes:** Timeout recovery is bounded to cooperative cancellation settlement at the timeout boundary and to the active safety-wrapper acceptance window through the native commit continuation. Non-timeout aborts still reject promptly, non-settling compactions still reject with `Compaction timed out`, late timeout-aborted results after wrapper rejection are ignored by `AgentSession`, and the default 180s timeout is unchanged.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/compaction-partial-summary.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.compaction-safety-timeout.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts`, and `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Regression test scenarios: a two-chunk compaction where chunk 1 succeeds and chunk 2 throws `TimeoutError` must return the chunk 1 summary plus a `[Partial summary: ...]` marker; a compaction canceled by outer timeout and immediately resolving with progress must return that progress instead of `Compaction timed out`; direct native compaction passes the safety timeout reason into `activeSession.abortCompaction(reason)` so timeout-aborted results can be committed only while the safety wrapper still accepts that reason; a late result after wrapper rejection must not remain accepted; a preflight compaction timeout must surface the timeout reason and config guidance.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The regression tests exercise the source owner boundaries directly and keep existing abort/timeout tests in place so timeout recovery cannot convert user cancellation or hung compaction into success.
- **Out of scope:** This PR does not change the default 180s timeout, add persistent checkpoint storage, change the shape/default of `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds`, alter compaction chunk planning, or change model/provider retry policy.

## Root Cause

`src/agents/compaction.ts` treated timeout errors the same as cancellation and rethrew immediately before attaching the already-generated summary to the error. `summarizeWithFallback()` therefore had no partial summary to reuse, even when earlier chunks had already completed successfully.

The outer safety timeout added a second loss path: `compactWithSafetyTimeout()` raced native compaction against a timeout rejection. On timeout it aborted the active compaction, but the timeout rejection could win before the native compaction settled with the partial result it produced during that cancellation.

The native caller added a third loss path: `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirectOnce()` canceled the real `AgentSession` via `activeSession.abortCompaction()` with no timeout reason, and `AgentSession.runCompactionWork()` discarded any compact result once its internal compaction signal was aborted. Timeout cancellation and user/request abort therefore collapsed into the same aborted state.

Separately, `buildPreflightCompactionFailureText()` hid the preflight compaction reason unless verbose details were enabled. That made a 180s compaction timeout look like a generic unrecoverable compaction failure and did not point users at the configured timeout knob.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Later chunk timeout and outer wall-clock safety timeout no longer discard already-generated compaction summary progress; preflight compaction timeout replies now show the timeout reason and `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds` guidance.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw worktrees. Original wall-clock/runtime proof was collected on `/media/vdc/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-92043`, branch `feat/issue-92043`; latest conflict-resolution verification was collected on `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-92899`, head `04c292a2ebc44f3fdac9a982803ee3d1c22a7efe` after rebasing through `origin/main` `9aa4250c58ad466856b5f1d77250ad5fecf2b70e`; latest drift check against `origin/main` `d71a24f3a4b7a03c060e01993afbb201cd024d26` reports `has_conflicts=false`, `overlap_files=[]`, and `sync_main_required=false`.

target.title: fix(matrix): normalize message fields and deduplicate streaming m.replace events for CLI display
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Matrix `message read` and `message pins` CLI output renders completely empty tables — all four columns (Time, Author, Text, Id) are blank because the formatter doesn't recognize Matrix-native field names. Additionally, Matrix blocked streaming produces one `m.replace` event per edit chunk in the room timeline, so `readMatrixMessages` returns 8+ intermediate edits per message, flooding the table with stale in-progress versions. **Problem 1 — blank table**: Matrix plugin returns messages with fields `eventId` / `sender` / `body` / `timestamp:number`, but the shared CLI formatter `renderMessageList` expects `id` / `authorTag` / `content` / `ts:ISOString`. Zero field overlap → all rows blank. **Problem 2 — streaming noise**: Each `m.replace` edit chunk is a real event in the Matrix timeline. Without dedup, a single blocked-stream response produces 8+ rows of intermediate edits plus the now-stale original. ## Why This Change Was Made 1. **`tool-actions.ts`**: Added `normalizeMatrixMessagesForFormatter()` — maps Matrix-native fields (`eventId` → `id`, `sender` → `authorTag`, `body` → `content`, `timestamp:number` → `ts:ISOString`) additively. Original fields are preserved so `--json` consumers keep the full Matrix payload. `listPins` preserves the raw `events` field alongside the new formatter-friendly `pins` field. 2. **`summary.ts`**: `summarizeMatrixRawEvent` now prefers `m.new_content` over `content.body` for `m.replace` events — the outer `content.body` is a fallback string for clients that don't understand edits, while `m.new_content` carries the authoritative edit body per the Matrix spec. 3. **`messages.ts`**: Added `m.replace` dedup in `readMatrixMessages` — uses timestamp comparison with `event_id` lexicographic tie-break, correct for both backward and forward pagination. Filters out `m.replace` events that lack `m.new_content` (invalid per Matrix spec). Validates that the `m.replace` sender matches the original event sender — cross-sender replacements do not suppress the original message. Both changes are Matrix-plugin-internal. No shared formatter, other channel, or SDK contract changes. **Note on `--json` semantics**: Dedup operates at the payload level in `readMatrixMessages`, so all consumers (CLI text, `--json`, agent tool results) receive the deduped `messages` array. This is intentional — leaving 8+ intermediate edit chunks in the JSON output would force every consumer to reimplement the same dedup logic. The raw Matrix event stream remains available via `--json` cursors (`nextBatch`/`prevBatch`) for consumers that need the unfiltered timeline. ## Evidence - Matrix test suite: 123 files, 1433 tests, 0 failures - 10 new regression tests: backward/forward pagination dedup, equal-timestamp tie-break, cross-sender m.replace rejection, invalid m.replace filtering, non-replace message preservation, pins JSON/formatter output shape, m.new_content body priority, fallback when m.new_content absent - Live verification against a real Matrix homeserver: ``` $ node openclaw.mjs message read --target '!yXceimCycQeAB0mmtz:matrix-local.hiclaw.io:18080' --channel matrix Messages ┌──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┐ │ Time │ Author │ Text │ Id │ ├──────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 2026-07-02T10:08:32.725Z │ @auth-test:matrix-loc… │ * 今天是 **2026年7月2日（星期四）**。 │ $hB8eLm7xXtRC33Rzb5Mi… │ │ 2026-07-02T10:08:29.129Z │ @cat:matrix-lo… │ @auth-test 💕: 今天日期 │ $pQx5zXyXmIy2UfZNva96… │ │ 2026-07-02T10:05:57.762Z │ @auth-test:matrix-loc… │ * 收到！看起来像是一个认证代码：`111`。 │ $Z3tGa3ob-TdTu8_Lq-_6… │ │ │ │ 你是想让我帮你用这个代码做些什么吗？比如登录某个服务、验证身份，或者是测试消息？告诉我具体需求，我来 │ │ │ │ │ 帮你处理。 │ │ │ 2026-07-02T10:05:20.401Z │ @cat:matrix-lo… │ @auth-test 💕: 111 │ $vZAP9RDAkTvhldkm7eMl… │ │ 2026-06-30T02:41:05.461Z │ @cat:matrix-lo… │ @auth-test 💕: sdfsdf │ $Evxee3Tm4TPrI8SvqMPe… │ └──────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘ ``` - Before/after comparison: on `main`, same command returns blank table. With this fix, all four columns render correctly. Streaming intermediate edits (8+ m.replace events for "收到…认证代码") collapsed to a single row showing the final version. ## User Impact - **Before**: `openclaw message read --channel matrix --target ` → fully blank table - **Before**: `openclaw message pins --channel matrix --target ` → malformed table - **After**: Table renders Time, Author, Text, Id correctly - **After**: Streaming edits deduped — one row per message (the final version), works for both backward and forward pagination - **After**: Cross-sender `m.replace` events do not suppress the original message (Matrix spec sender ownership enforced) - **After**: `--json` output preserves all original Matrix fields including `events` for `list-pins`

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk in the Google Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh path. Gemini CLI OAuth calls already cap HTTP bodies at 16 MiB via `fetchWithTimeout`, but `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` in the Vertex ADC refresh flow still buffered the full token response with `response.arrayBuffer()`. A faulty or hostile OAuth endpoint could stream an oversized refresh body and grow gateway memory without bound.

Related: #98507 covers the same bug class with additional gzip/decompression hardening.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vertex ADC refresh path now uses the shared bounded response reader (`readResponseWithLimit`) and reuses `GOOGLE_OAUTH_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB) from `oauth.http.ts` so the cap stays consistent across Google OAuth call sites.

This follows the same invariant as recent Google provider hardening work (for example #98692 on embedding batch reads): legitimate small token responses keep working, but unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

Scope is intentionally narrow:

- export the shared 16 MiB OAuth body cap from `oauth.http.ts`
- replace the bare `arrayBuffer()` read in `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload`
- add focused regression tests for normal refresh and oversized streamed bodies

This PR does not change ADC discovery, cache behavior, gzip decode policy, or non-OAuth Vertex auth flows.

## User Impact

Users running Google Vertex with `authorized_user` ADC keep the same refresh behavior for normal token responses (typically well under 10 KiB). If a refresh response exceeds 16 MiB, the gateway now fails fast with a clear error instead of buffering the entire body into memory.

## Evidence

Shared bounded-read wire proof: `oauth.http.test.ts` exercises the same `readResponseWithLimit` helper this PR uses on the Vertex ADC path against a local `http.createServer` listener on `127.0.0.1` with real `fetch()` and streamed chunked bodies. No mocked reader.

```text
stdout | extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > caps an oversized body streamed chunked over real wire
[oauth.http loopback proof] oversized path: cap=16777216 reported=16842704 server_total=18874368

stdout | extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > returns a Buffer for normal-size responses on real wire
[oauth.http loopback proof] normal path: cap=16777216 returned=45 body="{\"access_token\":\"loopback\",\"expires_in\":3600}"
```

Targeted unit proof: the new tests drive the production `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders` -> `refreshGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAccessToken` -> `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` path with real `Response` streams passed through an injected `fetchImpl`. They cover the normal authorized_user refresh case and the oversized streamed refresh body case that previously relied on unbounded `arrayBuffer()`.

```text
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts > vertex-adc OAuth token response bounds > rejects oversized token refresh bodies instead of buffering the whole stream

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.15s
```

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/google/oauth.http.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.oauth-response.test.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
```


Notes for reviewers:

- The 16 MiB cap matches the existing Google OAuth HTTP helper in `oauth.http.ts`. Legitimate ADC token responses are far smaller; the cap is a fail-closed bound against unbounded wire reads, not a product limit change.
- This PR intentionally does not include the gzip `maxOutputLength` hardening present in #98507. If maintainers prefer one combined fix, that sibling PR is the broader option; this one is the minimal shared-cap alignment for the ADC refresh read site.
- This PR does not add or migrate persistent state.

AI-assisted: built with Codex. I understand the change: it replaces the unbounded Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh `arrayBuffer()` read with the shared 16 MiB bounded response reader and adds focused regression tests for normal and oversized streamed refresh bodies.

Return `code.trim()` from `readConnectErrorDetailCode()` so normalized detail codes match canonical constants and structured formatting paths run for untrusted gateway error details.

target.title: fix(gateway): redact Responses media blocks in chat history sanitization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing chat history in Control UI / WebChat would still receive embedded `data:` image payloads on Responses-style media blocks (`input_image.image_url` and legacy `image.url`) after history sanitization, even though other base64 and data-URL media paths were already redacted.

Also fixes CI failures in `chat.directive-tags.test.ts`: live WebChat broadcast must keep `{ type: "input_image", image_url: "data:..." }` for QR/image delivery, so inline media redaction is scoped to history-only paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock()` now treats Responses media blocks the same as existing image/audio redaction when `redactInlineMedia: true` is passed from history paths only. Data URLs are removed from the projected history payload, replaced with `omitted: true` plus a byte count, while non-`data:` http(s) URLs remain intact for display/linking. Live broadcast via `projectChatDisplayMessages` keeps the default (`redactInlineMedia: false`) so inline images are preserved.

All chat.history-style callers now opt in: main gateway (`chat.ts`), session SSE snapshots (`session-history-state.ts`), embedded gateway stub, and TUI embedded backend.

## User Impact

Chat history fetched through the gateway, embedded agent tools, or TUI no longer leaks inline base64 image data for WebChat Responses `input_image` blocks or data-URL `image.url` blocks. Operators and users still see that media was present (via `omitted` + `bytes`) without shipping the raw payload over the wire. Remote https image links continue to display normally. Live WebChat broadcasts (QR codes, media replies) continue to deliver `input_image` data URLs to the client.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```text
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts -- -t "sanitizeChatHistoryMessages"
# 12 passed

pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts -- -t "broadcast|input_image|media"
# 90 passed

pnpm test src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts -- -t "chat.history"
# 11 passed

pnpm test src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts -- -t "embedded TUI history"
# 1 passed (redactInlineMedia asserted on loadHistory)
```

New/updated cases cover:
- sanitizer shapes: `input_image.image_url`, `image.url`, `image.source.data`, nested `image_url.url`, https preservation, broadcast preservation
- embedded gateway stub: all `chat.history` projection calls pass `redactInlineMedia: true`
- TUI embedded backend: `loadHistory` passes `redactInlineMedia: true` to `projectRecentChatDisplayMessages`

### Real behavior proof (outside Vitest)

```text
node --import tsx scripts/proof-chat-history-sanitize-input-image.mjs
# All proof checks passed (8 cases including projectRecentChatDisplayMessages history path)
```

target.title: fix(android): stop talk mode audio capture on background
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Android app moves to the background (`MainActivity.onStop()` → `NodeRuntime.setForeground(false)`), TalkMode continuous realtime audio capture (`AudioRecord`) keeps running. The microphone indicator stays on and audio frames continue streaming to the gateway via `talk.session.appendAudio`.

The root cause is `setForeground(false)` calls `stopManualVoiceSession()`, which is guarded to only stop `VoiceCaptureMode.ManualMic` — when TalkMode is active, it returns immediately without stopping anything:

```
NodeRuntime.kt:1804  stopManualVoiceSession()
                       → if (mode != ManualMic) return  // TalkMode: no-op
```

Meanwhile, the TalkMode realtime capture loop (`TalkModeManager.kt:750`) checks `_isEnabled` but never checks `_isForeground`, so `AudioRecord.read()` continues uninterrupted.

This is inconsistent with the PTT background gate added in `e3f46d0926` (#98055), which explicitly blocks starting new Talk captures from the background but does not stop already-running continuous capture.

## Why This Change Was Made

A new method `stopVoiceCaptureForBackground()` replaces `stopManualVoiceSession()` in `setForeground(false)`. Unlike the old method (which only stops ManualMic), the new method stops **any** active voice capture mode — both ManualMic and TalkMode — by delegating to the existing `setVoiceCaptureMode(VoiceCaptureMode.Off)` stop chain.

The approach is minimal (1 file, +7/-1), reuses the proven `setVoiceCaptureMode(Off)` path that already correctly stops TalkMode's `realtimeCaptureJob` → `AudioRecord.stop()/release()` and `realtimeAppendJob` → audio frame streaming. No new stop logic or state machine added.

`stopManualVoiceSession()` is preserved for its existing caller `setVoiceScreenActive(false)` (in-app navigation away from the voice screen), where only stopping ManualMic is appropriate.

## User Impact

- **Affected users**: Anyone using Android TalkMode (continuous conversation mode) who switches to another app or the home screen
- **Before**: microphone indicator and foreground service continue; TalkMode keeps capturing and streaming audio in the background
- **After**: TalkMode stops cleanly on background, same as ManualMic; microphone indicator and foreground service are removed

## Evidence

- Code path analysis: traced full call chain from `MainActivity.onStop()` → `NodeRuntime.setForeground(false)` → `stopManualVoiceSession()` no-op → `TalkModeManager.realtimeCaptureJob` continuing (see analysis above)
- Review: `openclaw-pr-review` passed with P2-only findings (test gap — Android Gradle unavailable in this environment; fix path proven through `setVoiceCaptureMode(Off)` stop chain that is tested indirectly via `talkPttStart_rejectsNewCaptureWhenBackgrounded`)
- Android Gradle tests could not run locally (network restriction on Gradle download); the fix reuses the existing `setVoiceCaptureMode(Off)` → `talkMode.setEnabled(false)` → `TalkModeManager.stop()` → `stopRealtimeRelay()` → `realtimeCaptureJob.cancel()` chain that is the same path exercised by normal TalkMode disable

Behavior addressed: TalkMode AudioRecord continues after app background
Real environment tested: N/A (code-path verification)
Exact steps or command run after this patch: In-app TalkMode active → press Home → verify mic indicator disappears, AudioRecord stopped
Evidence after fix: N/A (requires Android device/emulator with Gradle build)
Observed result after fix: Pending real-device validation
What was not tested: Real-device background transition with TalkMode active (Gradle build unavailable in this environment)

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve legacy reseed attachments
target.body:

## What Problem This Solves

Legacy Claude CLI reseed rows can contain an empty `<next_user_message>` text block alongside an image, document, or other native user content. The importer returned `null` for the whole row, hiding those sibling blocks from visible OpenClaw history.

The importer now applies one invariant to receipt-backed and legacy reseed rows: remove only the proven synthetic text block, and drop the row only when no content remains.

Scalar and single-text-block empty reseeds keep their existing suppression behavior. Mixed native content preserves sibling order and bytes.

## User Impact

Image-only and attachment-bearing legacy Claude turns remain visible after reseed import instead of disappearing with the empty synthetic wrapper.
